title: Building Ebyafaayo: an offline Luganda family-history keeper with Gemma 4 and Sunbird ASR

content.text:
My build spec for the agent (ebyafaayo-agent-prompt.md):

# Build Prompt: Ebyafaayo, an offline family oral history keeper

You are helping me build a brand-new project for the DEV Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge, Week 4: "Ghost in the Machine". The theme is to build something that honors the past, in the spirit of Día de los Muertos, using open-weight models or open-source AI. The open AI pieces must be what makes the project work.

**Deadline: October 31, 11:59 PM PDT (Sunday 1 November, 9:59 AM Kampala time).** We have about two days. A small project that works and is easy to demo beats a big one that breaks.

Read this whole file, then show me a short plan before writing code.

## The idea

Ebyafaayo (Luganda for "history" or "past events") helps a family record an elder telling a story in Luganda and turns it into a written family memory, fully offline on a laptop. Nothing is sent to the cloud.

The flow:

1. Ask the elder for consent, then record a story (or upload an audio file).
2. An open Luganda speech model transcribes it.
3. The family checks and corrects the transcript (people must stay in control; elders' words matter).
4. Gemma 4, running locally through Ollama, turns the corrected transcript into a structured memory: a title, the story in clean Luganda, an English version, the people mentioned and how they are related, places, time periods, clan (ekika) and totem (omuziro) only if mentioned, proverbs, and gentle follow-up questions to ask the elder next time.
5. Memories are grouped into a remembrance page for each ancestor or elder, with a simple timeline.
6. Export a printable "memory book" (save as PDF from the browser).

## Hard rules (challenge rules)

1. **New project, new repo.** Create a new public GitHub repo named `ebyafaayo` today. All code must be written within the challenge window. Do not copy code from Eddembe or any other project of mine. Using open-source libraries is fine.
2. **Open AI must be central.** Use only open-weight models and open-source tools for the AI parts. Do not use any closed or paid AI API (no Gemini API, no OpenAI, no Sunbird hosted API).
3. **Credit prior work** in the README: Gemma 4 (Google DeepMind, open weights), Sunbird AI's open ASR model, Ollama, and any library or code snippet that is non-trivial.
4. **Licence:** MIT for our code. List the model licences separately (Gemma's terms, the Sunbird model's MIT licence).

## Hard rules (honesty and respect)

1. **Gemma must never invent family facts.** It may only use what is in the transcript. If a name, place, date, clan or relationship is not clearly said, leave it empty or mark it "unclear". Never guess a clan or totem.
2. **Every structured field links back to the transcript**: store the sentence it came from, and show it on hover or tap.
3. **The family can edit everything** before saving: transcript, translation and every field.
4. **Consent first.** Before recording, show a short consent screen: who is speaking, that the recording stays on this computer, and a checkbox the family ticks. Store the consent with the recording.
5. **Private by default.** No analytics, no telemetry, no external requests after the models are downloaded. Say so in the app and README.

## Tech stack

Keep it simple and local:

- **Backend:** Python 3.11+, FastAPI, SQLite (via SQLModel or plain `sqlite3`). Audio files stored in a local `data/` folder (git-ignored).
- **Speech to text:** `Sunbird/asr-whisper-large-v3-salt` from Hugging Face (MIT, adapted from Whisper Large v3, supports Luganda with language code `lug`, plus Acholi, Lugbara, Ateso, Runyankole, Rutooro, Lumasaba, Lusoga, Swahili, Kinyarwanda and English). Load it with `transformers` using the Whisper processor and model classes as shown on its model card at https://salt.sunbird.ai/models/asr-whisper-large-v3-salt/. Use the language token from the model card; do not guess it. Split long audio into chunks of up to 30 seconds. If the model is gated on Hugging Face, tell me so I can accept the terms and log in.
- **Reasoning and translation:** Gemma 4 through Ollama (`ollama pull gemma4:e4b` to start). Ollama lists `gemma4:e2b`, `gemma4:e4b`, `gemma4:26b` and `gemma4:31b`. Check my laptop's RAM and GPU and recommend the largest that runs at a usable speed. Use the Ollama Python client or its local HTTP API with JSON output, and validate with Pydantic. Retry once with a "fix this JSON" call if it breaks.
- **Optional test:** Gemma 4 E2B and E4B accept audio up to 30 seconds and are trained for multilingual speech recognition. Spend at most 30 minutes testing whether Gemma 4 can transcribe a short Luganda clip, through Ollama if audio works there or through `transformers` as the Gemma audio docs show (https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/capabilities/audio). Compare it with the Sunbird model on the same clip and keep whichever is better. Write the result honestly in the README, even if Gemma loses.
- **Frontend:** React + Vite + TypeScript with MUI (Material Design), served by the backend for the demo. Warm, respectful design: deep earthy colours (for example bark-cloth brown `#6D4C41`, deep green `#1B5E20`, warm cream background `#FBF7F0`), a serif font for story text (for example Lora or EB Garamond from Google Fonts, bundled locally so it works offline), sans-serif for controls. Mobile friendly.
- **Recording:** browser `MediaRecorder`; convert to 16 kHz mono WAV on the server with `ffmpeg` before transcription.

## Gemma prompt (structure step)

Put prompts in `backend/prompts/`. The structure prompt must say, in plain words:

- You are helping a Ugandan family preserve an elder's story. Use only the transcript below. Do not add any fact that is not in it.
- Keep the elder's own words in the Luganda version; only fix obvious transcription errors and punctuation, and list every change you made.
- Translate faithfully into simple English. If a word has no clear English meaning, keep the Luganda word and explain it in brackets.
- If something is unclear, return it as unclear. Never guess names, clans, totems, dates or relationships.
- For each extracted item, include the exact source sentence from the transcript.
- Suggest 3 to 5 gentle follow-up questions in Luganda and English, about things the elder mentioned but did not explain.

Output JSON with: `title`, `luganda_text`, `english_text`, `changes_made[]`, `people[]` (name, relationship_to_speaker, source_sentence, confidence), `places[]`, `time_periods[]`, `clan` and `totem` (each with value, source_sentence, or null), `proverbs[]` (luganda, english, source_sentence), `follow_up_questions[]` (luganda, english).

## Screens

1. **Home:** the family's elders and ancestors as cards (name, photo optional, number of stories). "Record a new story" button.
2. **Consent and record:** consent checkbox, speaker name, language (default Luganda), big record button with timer, or upload a file.
3. **Review transcript:** audio player next to the editable transcript. Show progress while transcribing (it can be slow on CPU).
4. **Memory:** the structured result, all fields editable, each linked to its source sentence. Save.
5. **Remembrance page:** per person, their stories in order, people and places they mentioned, a simple timeline, and the follow-up questions still unanswered.
6. **Memory book:** print-friendly page for one person or the whole family. "Save as PDF" through the browser print dialog.
7. **About and privacy:** what runs locally, which open models are used, and the credits.

## Build order

Test each step before moving on, and tell me what to test.

1. Repo, FastAPI skeleton, React app, SQLite, `README` stub, MIT licence. Commit.
2. Ollama with Gemma 4 working from the backend on a sample Luganda text (use a short text I give you or a clearly marked sample).
3. Sunbird ASR transcribing a short Luganda clip. (The Sunbird SALT dataset on Hugging Face, `multispeaker-lug` config, has test audio if I have none yet.)
4. Record or upload, then transcribe, review and correct.
5. Structure with Gemma 4, edit, save.
6. Remembrance page and timeline.
7. Memory book export.
8. Optional Gemma audio test (30 minutes maximum).
9. Polish, README with screenshots, a one-command setup (`make setup` or a script), and a 1 to 2 minute demo video plan.

If time runs short, cut in this order: timeline, photos, Gemma audio test, memory book styling. Never cut consent, the source-sentence links, or editing.

## README must include

- The story behind the project (I will write this part; leave a placeholder).
- What it does, with screenshots.
- How it works: architecture diagram (Mermaid) showing browser, FastAPI, Sunbird ASR, Ollama with Gemma 4, SQLite, all on one laptop.
- Why open models: works offline, family stories stay private, free to run, can be improved for more Ugandan languages.
- Setup steps, hardware notes (RAM needed per Gemma size), and how long transcription takes on CPU.
- Limitations: Luganda transcription errors happen, translation is not perfect, so the family must review; clan and totem are only recorded when the elder says them.
- Credits and licences.

## Agent session

The challenge lets us share a saved agent session to show the process. Keep a clean log of the main steps and decisions so I can include it.

## When you are unsure

Ask me. I would rather answer a question than debug a wrong guess.

I've read the whole prompt and checked your laptop. Some of what I found changes the plan, so here it is before any code.

## What I found on your laptop

| | Status | Effect on the plan |
|---|---|---|
| **Disk** | **3.1 GB free** (99% full) | This blocks everything else. The Sunbird model alone is a 6.2 GB download, and Gemma needs about 4.5 GB more. |
| RAM | 7.6 GB total, about 1.8 GB free right now (VS Code, Brave and SQL Server use most of it) | Only one model can be loaded at a time. |
| CPU/GPU | i5-7300U, 4 threads, Intel integrated graphics only | Everything runs on the CPU, so it will be slow. |
| Node | v24 is installed through nvm | Fine. |
| ffmpeg, Python 3.12, gh (logged in as Nuwahereza-eng) | Installed | Fine. |
| Ollama | **Not installed** | You'll need to install it. |
| Hugging Face | No login. The Sunbird model is gated, but access is approved automatically once you accept its terms. | You'll need to accept the terms and log in. |

**Gemma choice: `gemma4:e2b`** (4.3–4.6 GB). `e4b` (6.6 GB) won't fit in your RAM next to anything else, and the 12B and larger models are out of reach. On this CPU, expect Gemma to take a few minutes per story. I'll measure the real time in step 2.

**Speech to text:** loading the Sunbird model the way its model card shows (`transformers`, full precision) needs about 6 GB of RAM and would be very slow on this CPU. My recommendation is to convert the same Sunbird weights once to an 8-bit version for `faster-whisper` (MIT licence). That would need about 1.5 GB of RAM and should be several times faster. It is still the same open Sunbird model, and I'd credit both in the README. Your prompt says to use `transformers`, though, so I need your OK before switching.

## Build plan (follows your build order)

1. **Skeleton:** create the public `ebyafaayo` repo in this folder, with FastAPI, SQLite (SQLModel), React + Vite + TypeScript + MUI, bundled Lora font, MIT licence and a README stub. Your two draft `.md` files stay out of git. Then commit.
2. **Gemma via Ollama:** a structure prompt in `backend/prompts/`, JSON output checked with Pydantic, and one "fix this JSON" retry. I'll test it on a clearly marked sample text and time it.
3. **Sunbird ASR:** read the language token from the model card, split audio into 30-second chunks, and test on a clip from SALT `multispeaker-lug`. I'll write down the real speed for the README.
4. **Consent → record/upload → transcribe:** ffmpeg converts to 16 kHz WAV, the progress shows while it runs, and the transcript is editable.
5. **Memory screen:** structure with Gemma, every field editable, the source sentence on hover/tap, then save.
6. **Remembrance page** with the timeline, and the follow-up questions that are still open.
7. **Memory book** that prints to PDF.
8. **Gemma audio test**, 30 minutes at most. With your RAM and disk this is the first thing I'd cut.
9. **Polish:** README (Mermaid diagram, hardware notes, limitations, credits), a `make setup` command, and a demo video plan.

Throughout, I'll keep `docs/agent-log.md` as the clean log of steps and decisions.

## What I need from you

1. **Free up disk space.** I'd like to delete three things: `~/.npm` (5.3 GB), `~/.cache/pip` (3.6 GB) and your Trash (0.4 GB). The first two are only download caches and rebuild themselves when needed. That brings free space to about 12 GB, which is just enough. OK to delete them?
2. **Install Ollama.** It needs sudo, so please run this yourself: `curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh`
3. **Hugging Face access.** Accept the terms at https://huggingface.co/Sunbird/asr-whisper-large-v3-salt, then run `pip install -U huggingface_hub && hf auth login` with a read token.
4. **Speech-to-text runtime.** Can I use the `faster-whisper` 8-bit conversion, or do you want to stick with `transformers` as the model card shows?
5. **Optional:** closing SQL Server (`sudo systemctl stop mssql-server`) frees about 300 MB of RAM while we work.

I can build step 1 now, since it doesn't depend on any of these, while you do 1–3. Should I start?

To your question about what was taking longer: Gemma got stuck in a loop, writing "ekyera ekyera ekyera…" for over 8 minutes on a job that should take about 3. I stopped it and added hard limits on output length, and the next run finished in 170 seconds.

The app now works end to end on your laptop, except for automatic speech recognition. Consent, recording, typing or correcting the transcript, the Gemma memory, editing, the remembrance page with its timeline, and the memory book all work. I checked every screen in a headless browser, desktop and mobile. All 11 backend tests pass. The work is in 4 local commits; nothing is on GitHub yet.

**What I tested and how it went:**
- **Gemma 4 E2B:** ran on a short sample Luganda story I wrote and labelled as invented. It found all four people with the right relationships (father, mother, husband), all three places, both time periods and the proverb. Every item matched a sentence in the transcript, and it invented no clan or totem.
- **Two changes made that work:**
  - Asking Gemma for everything in one call sometimes gave empty lists, so it now makes two smaller calls: one for the text and translation, one for the people, places and times.
  - Every field in Gemma's answer now has a length limit, which is what stopped the loop.
- **Problems that remain, written into the README:**
  - The translation once turned "that is where I met my husband" into "my husband was killed".
  - It never got the meaning of the proverb right.
  - The Luganda follow-up questions are often ungrammatical.

  The app can't detect translation errors, so the family's review matters most there.
- **Crashes:** the two session restarts were the system running out of memory. Ollama now runs on its own with a memory cap, so it can't take VS Code down with it.

**Not done:**
- **The Gemma audio test:** I cut it. Gemma in Ollama doesn't accept audio, and the other route needs about 10 GB more disk.
- **Speech recognition is still untested.** I need two things from you:
  1. Accept the terms at https://huggingface.co/Sunbird/asr-whisper-large-v3-salt and run `~/Ebyafaayo/.venv/bin/hf auth login`.
  2. Free about 2 more GB of disk; it needs about 7 GB and 5.8 GB is free. Chrome's cache (3.8 GB) is the easiest thing to clear.

  Then run `make asr-model` (or tell me to), and I'll test it on a Luganda clip from the Sunbird SALT test set and add the timings to the README.

**Blocked, for you to do:**
- **Create the GitHub repo.** The permission system blocked me from creating a public repo. From `~/Ebyafaayo`, run `gh repo create ebyafaayo --public --source . --push`.
- **Fix your git email.** It's set to `<email>`, without `.com`, so GitHub won't link the commits to your account. Fix it before pushing.

**Your own parts:**
- The story section at the top of [README.md](README.md).
- Check the name in [LICENSE](LICENSE); I put your GitHub handle, `Nuwahereza-eng`.
- Replace the sample screenshots with real ones once you've recorded a real story; [scripts/screenshots.sh](scripts/screenshots.sh) takes them.

The shot-by-shot video plan is in [docs/demo-video-plan.md](docs/demo-video-plan.md), and the session log for the challenge is in [docs/agent-log.md](docs/agent-log.md).

To run the app: `make run`, then open http://127.0.0.1:8000. Ollama is still running as a capped background service; stop it with `systemctl --user stop ebyafaayo-ollama`.
